sources.name: CBC Radio, The Sunday Edition
sources.text: walking-behaviour researcher Catrine Tudor-Locke (University of Massachusetts Amherst), on the Manpo-kei origin: 1965, Yamasa Tokei Keiki, a brand name and slogan rather than a tested health threshold.

sources.name: I-Min Lee
sources.text: (Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health), quoted on the launch: "There were no actual studies that had looked at '10,000 steps'"; the figure chosen because it sounded good.

sources.name: Lee IM et al.
sources.text: Association of Step Volume and Intensity With All-Cause Mortality in Older Women, JAMA Internal Medicine (2019): ~17,000 women, plateau ~7,500 steps/day, 7,500 equivalent to 10,000 for mortality risk; NIH Research Matters summary.

sources.name: Paluch AE et al.
sources.text: Daily steps and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis of 15 international cohorts, Lancet Public Health (2022): plateau, age-dependent (~6,000-8,000 older adults).

sources.name: Paluch AE et al.
sources.text: CARDIA study, JAMA Network Open (2021): middle-aged adults at ≥7,000 steps had 50-70% lower mortality than those below.

sources.name: Science World Report
sources.text: 'The 10,000 Steps-A-Day Challenge: History and Truth of the Exercise Routine' (2014): Shape Up America!, founded 1994 by Dr. C. Everett Koop, a former US Surgeon General, promoted the 10,000-steps-a-day recommendation in the United States.
